📚 Today you learned

Free Cash Flow Margin

You already know FCF (operating cash flow minus capex) — FCF margin just divides that by revenue, so you can compare quality across time or peers regardless of size. It's the number that's actually spooking GOOG right now: Alphabet's FCF margin reportedly collapsed from ~21% to ~9.2% as management guided full-year capex up to $180–190B chasing AI infrastructure. Revenue and even net income can keep climbing while FCF margin craters — that's the tell that a company has shifted from harvesting cash to reinvesting it heavily, with no guarantee the reinvestment pays off on the timeline the market wants. A shrinking FCF margin during a capex surge isn't automatically bearish (NVDA's suppliers all show it too), but paired with delayed monetization (YouTube AI revenue pushed to 2029) and talent departures, it reads as "the story got worse, not just the multiple." This is why the stock is testing its stop.

Also today: Capex intensity — capex as % of revenue; when it spikes faster than revenue guidance, FCF margin compression is mechanical, not optional.
